title: cluster status --json, v1
description: The output of `cluster status --json` and `cluster up --json`. This is a stability contract: any change to a field's name, type or presence requires a new file, status.v2.json, and a new value of the top-level `version`. Field names and optionality are taken from the json tags on fold.Result, fold.Phase and snapshot.Ref.

version.description: Schema version. The cluster's Kubernetes version is status.version, which keeps that name because it is fold.Result's json tag.

envelope.description: The snapshot the status was folded from, emitted with --verbose. Objects are raw Kubernetes JSON of a dozen kinds from three providers; this tool owns none of their schemas and does not constrain them.

elapsed_ns.description: How long the command has been watching, in nanoseconds.

stall.description: The one object worth looking at, present only when a phase is stalled.

estimates.description: Per-phase estimate from local history, keyed by phase name. Absent phases have no history.

result.description: fold.Result: one cluster folded into four phases at one instant.

class.description: spec.topology.class. Absent when the Cluster has no topology.

version.description: spec.topology.version, the cluster's Kubernetes version. Not the schema version.

placement.description: The value of the class's `placement` variable: self or hosted. Absent when the class does not expose it.

phases.description: Always four phases in fold.Order, or null when the envelope held no Cluster.

ready.description: True when every phase is done.

at.description: The instant the snapshot was read at, RFC 3339. On a replay this comes from _meta.t_plus_s, not from the wall clock.

elapsed_ns.description: Now minus the Cluster's creationTimestamp, in nanoseconds. Zero when either is unknown.

phase.description: fold.Phase: one of the four user-facing phases.

state.description: stalled is running with no condition transition on any contributing object for longer than the stall threshold.

detail.description: The one thing worth showing next to the phase: "2/3 nodes", "hosted", "no workers".

elapsed_ns.description: How long the phase has been running, or how long it took, in nanoseconds.

last_transition.description: The most recent condition change on any contributing object, RFC 3339. Absent when no contributing object has ever transitioned; stall detection is entirely about this field.

started_at.description: When the previous phase finished, RFC 3339. Absent when that is unknown.

contributors.description: Every object whose conditions were read for this phase. Null when the phase has none, which is how "no workers" and "addons: none" appear.

ref.description: snapshot.Ref: one object, named the way a user sees it in a stall line.

group.description: API group without the version, e.g. controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io. Absent for core objects.

estimate.description: p50 and p95 over the last runs of one phase. known is false below three samples, and then the renderer says so instead of showing a number.

condition.description: A condition from either API generation, normalised. deprecated is true when it was read from status.deprecated.v1beta1.conditions.

candidate.description: One False condition that was considered. lost_to is empty on the winner and otherwise names the rule that decided it.

stall.description: The ranked answer to 'what is this waiting on'. condition_type is the raw CAPI condition name and is jargon: it belongs on the raw line and under --verbose only.

raw.description: A kubectl command that prints the object this line names.
